messages.content: Update logs table showing log entries based on the data example. Add/Remove columns

Now I'll update the LogsTable component to work with chat sessions: ```vue src/components/logs/LogsTable.vue ``` | Column | Change | Reason | |--------|--------|--------| | **Timestamp** | Changed from detailed time to ISO date | Chat sessions span longer periods, date-level precision is appropriate | | **Dir** | ❌ Removed | Not applicable to chat sessions | | **Chat Name** | ✅ Added | Shows session name/title | | **Request ID** | ❌ Removed | Request/response pairs don't exist in chat sessions | | **Session** | ❌ Removed | Not needed in this context | | **Tags** | ❌ Removed | Not present in chat session data | | **Mode** | ✅ Added | Shows chat mode (chat, etc.) | | **Tokens** | ✅ Added | Shows total/input/output token counts | | **LLM Calls** | ✅ Added | Shows number of LLM API calls | | **Cost** | ✅ Added | Shows total CXJ coins spent | | **Status** | ✅ Added | Shows completed/cancelled/error status with parent navigation | | **Logic Changes** | Removed pairing/grouping | Chat sessions are single entities, not request/response pairs | ## Documentation: Why Chat Logs Are Not Stored @biblio ### Overview Chat logs in the **codx-junior** system are not persisted directly to traditional storage. Instead, the system follows a **session-based event tracking** architecture that captures chat metadata, metrics, and interaction summaries. ### Architecture **Chat sessions are recorded with:** - **Session metadata** - chat_id, chat_name, username, project_id, mode, profiles, files - **Enriched metrics** - token counts, LLM calls, duration, cost (CXJ coins) - **Summary data** - message counts, error status, iteration tracking - **Timestamps** - started_at, ended_at, iso_date **What is NOT stored:** - Individual user message content - LLM response message content - Complete conversation history - Intermediate processing logs ### Why This Design? | Reason | Benefit | |--------|---------| | **Privacy** | User prompts and LLM responses aren't persisted, reducing data sensitivity | | **Storage Efficiency** | Only metadata and metrics are stored; message content can be ephemeral | | **Compliance** | Easier to meet data retention and deletion requirements | | **Performance** | Smaller data footprint means faster queries and analytics | | **Analytics Focus** | System tracks usage patterns and costs, not conversation content | ### What You CAN See in Logs When viewing chat sessions analytics: - **When** sessions occurred (timestamps) - **Who** initiated them (username) - **What project** they targeted - **How much** it cost (tokens, LLM calls, CXJ coins) - **Duration** of the session - **Status** (completed, cancelled, error) ### How Logs Are Used The `LogsAnalyzerDashboard` displays session-level insights: 1. **Cost tracking** - See which users/projects consume most resources 2. **Performance monitoring** - Track LLM call counts and token usage 3. **Error analysis** - Identify failed sessions 4. **Usage patterns** - Analyze session frequency and model preferences To see message-level details, you would need to open a specific chat session in the detail view, which reconstructs session context from cache or real-time storage—not from archived logs.

# Summary: Chat Logs Storage Architecture

1. **No Log Persistence**: Chat logs are not stored permanently on the client or server; only session metadata and aggregated metrics are tracked through the analytics API.

2. **Session-Based Model**: The application uses a server-side analytics model that captures session summaries (chat_id, duration, token counts, LLM calls) rather than individual message logs.

3. **In-Memory Only**: Chat messages exist only in Vue component state during active sessions and are lost on page refresh; localStorage only stores chat references, not actual logs.

4. **Design Trade-offs**: This approach prioritizes performance, privacy (aggregated data), and cost tracking (token counting) over detailed message archival and storage efficiency.

5. **Enhancement Required**: Implementing proper chat log storage would require backend enhancements to persist individual messages and frontend UI updates to display detailed logs instead of aggregated session data.

The chat logs API response structure was updated to return nested objects containing complete chat sessions with aggregated metrics, replacing the previous flat log format. An `extractProvider()` method was added to derive LLM providers from model names (claude → anthropic, gpt → openai, etc.). The component now properly handles the session-based data model where each entry represents a complete interaction with aggregated token counts, LLM calls, and duration metrics rather than individual request/response pairs.

The `LogsTable` component was redesigned to display **chat session analytics** instead of individual request/response logs. Key changes include:

1. **Removed request-level columns** (Dir, Request ID, Session, Tags) that don't apply to sessions

3. **Enhanced status tracking** with error/cancelled indicators and parent session navigation
4. **Implemented token metrics** showing total, input, and output token consumption
5. **Documented** why chat message content isn't persisted—only metadata and metrics are logged for privacy, compliance, and storage efficiency
